clue.text: Quiet game

definitions.meaning: an old word for hushed or silent, as in keeping still and saying nothing
a card game for four players in two partnerships, ancestor of bridge

explanation.surface: A request for a calm, peaceful pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: an archaic adjective meaning silent, and the name of a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Gag fashion expert

parts.note: wise is an old noun for manner or way, as in 'in no wise'
a crack shot or crack player is an expert one

explanation.surface: A joke told by someone who knows all about clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like clothing, but here it means manner, the old noun wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is a joke, and a smart quip is the same thing.

clue.text: I stick within hearing of the White House

indicators.note: within hearing says the next word is to be taken by its sound alone

parts.note: to stick is to glue

explanation.surface: Someone attaching themselves near the US president's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The White House is not Washington's but any house made of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow dwelling is a house that is white all over.

clue.text: Matron's solved one across light

indicators.note: solved suggests a puzzle worked out, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hospital matron has worked out the answer to a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One across' seems to be a crossword reference, but it is a light (window) set across, above a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight over a door sits on a horizontal crossbar, and the word names both bar and window.

clue.text: Athlete one may take to one's heart

definitions.meaning: a runner who sets the speed for others in a race

definitions.text: one may take to one's heart
definitions.meaning: a medical device fitted to regulate heartbeat

explanation.surface: A sportsman someone could grow very fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take to one's heart' sounds like affection; read literally it is an implant.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers a race runner setting the tempo and an electronic device implanted to keep the heart beating regularly.

clue.text: Pickle, soft and easily digested

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for soft
a light meal is one easily digested

explanation.surface: A preserve that is mild and kind to the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like a food in the surface, but it means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is to be in a sorry state or predicament.

clue.text: Officer on North Island supplies building material

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A military officer on an island provides supplies for construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of cement, sand and gravel used in construction.

clue.text: Gruesome vehicle in Tom Pearse's transport

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the animal

parts.note: in the folk song Widecombe Fair, Tom Pearse lends his old grey mare
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A grim carriage carried by a character from a folk song.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Pearse is from the English folk song Widecombe Fair, about the old grey mare he lent to a crowd of riders.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ghastly, dwelling on death and horror.

clue.text: The snake gives sovereign firm support

parts.note: a king is a sovereign ruler
CO is short for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A serpent provides the monarch with solid backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A large venomous Asian serpent, the longest of its kind.

clue.text: Sculptor portrays river god

parts.note: Odin is the chief Norse god

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a deity of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: Yeoman to the rescue

parts.note: yeoman service means sterling help, and help that comes to the rescue is deliverance from danger

explanation.surface: A loyal yeoman rides up to save the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeoman service is a stock phrase for good help, so the clue is a roundabout picture of being saved.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescue from harm or loss is deliverance, the help that arrives in time.

clue.text: Punished with prison newspaper boss

parts.note: can is slang for prison
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone jailed alongside a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten with a stick as a punishment, as once in schools.

clue.text: Commit oneself, but not directly one's birth occurs

indicators.note: not directly says the letters do not go straight, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a commitment while their child arrives by an indirect route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not directly' rearranges ONES BIRTH OCCURS; the surface looks like a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossed this river into Italy and could not turn back, so the idiom means taking an irrevocable step.

clue.text: "Don's a donkey", you said to me

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells me a university don is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, but it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, to take on a garment.

clue.text: Blue locomotive, a high-flier

parts.note: the sky is the blue
Stephenson's Rocket was an early locomotive

explanation.surface: A blue engine that is very ambitious.
explanation.definitionFit: A firework that soars upwards, high in the air.

clue.text: All of a doodah, Albert and me, really upset

indicators.note: upset suggests knocking things over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Albert and I are thoroughly distressed and in a dither.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All of a doodah' is British slang for flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of nervous excitement means quivering or trembling.

clue.text: After physical education pass on in next change of shift

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
change of says the word next is rearranged
after puts the dying after the PE

parts.note: to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: Following a gym class, someone hands over to the next crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' rearranges NEXT to EXNT, which goes round PEDIE. 'Shift' is a noun meaning a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a makeshift means to an end, a convenient resource.

clue.text: For his part, South quits bar

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: quits removes one letter from the word his

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: For his contribution, a man named South leaves the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is the verb to forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban or forbid something is to bar it.

clue.text: Vital committee on which 27 shone

parts.note: key means vital, essential
a board is a committee

explanation.surface: An essential panel on which a composer excelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is the composer, a celebrated piano virtuoso.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano's row of keys, where the Hungarian virtuoso dazzled audiences.

clue.text: Peccadillo pertaining to a criminal

parts.note: of means belonging or pertaining to
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: A minor sin related to a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin, a minor misdeed.

clue.text: Returning in the afternoon, spots pitch

indicators.note: returning reads both pieces back to front, in one run

parts.note: PM is post meridiem, in the afternoon
acne is spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone comes back in the afternoon and notices a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch tents is to set up camp.

clue.text: It's vital to end fuel mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up is a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Avoiding a fuel confusion is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessary, required, essential.

clue.text: Not even Ruth loses head in quiz

parts.note: odd numbers are not even

indicators.note: loses head drops the first letter of the word for ruth

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity

explanation.surface: Ruth gets a quiz question wrong, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name but is the old word for pity. 'Quiz' is an old word for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz once meant an odd or eccentric person, a curiosity.

clue.text: Divers do cut up rough

definitions.meaning: swimmers plunge from the far end of a pool
British phrase for losing one's temper

explanation.surface: Swimmers behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally plunging into water out of one's depth, and figuratively losing self-control in anger.

clue.text: Dancing girl goes to work

definitions.note: the definition names the activity, the answer a dance

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A girl dancer goes to her job.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in quick time.

clue.text: Cut up writing papers

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word read upwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
MS is a manuscript, writing

explanation.surface: Someone tears writing paper to shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: Test papers set to examine students.

clue.text: Left with President a point to compare

parts.note: Ike was President Eisenhower
N is a compass point

explanation.surface: Left with the President, someone looks for a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken is to draw a comparison or similarity.

clue.text: Paper bag

parts.note: a brief is a barrister's paper
a case is a bag

explanation.surface: A bag made of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: it is a bag for papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat case for carrying documents.

clue.text: With endurance uncommon in Latin type

indicators.note: uncommon suggests unusual, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rare typeface in Latin that endures.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something tolerantly and without complaint.

clue.text: He composed "Hark! hark!"

indicators.note: the second hark asks us to listen, taking the word by its sound

parts.note: list is an old word for listen, hark

explanation.surface: A composer wrote a cry to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hark' is both the word sounded and the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian composer and pianist.
